svg.title: CHISUM: Stern ramp: electrical installation, JS3-304 revision 1
svg.text: Stern ramp: electrical installation, sheet 3 of 4 · JS3-304 · revision 1 · 12 November 2026
From where the generating sets are to stand to the last terminal of the control stand. What is not installed is drawn broken and its place is marked in the model.
Cable sizes in mm² of copper. Places: metres to port, from the transom, above the keel.
MSB 690 V (place marked: main switchboard room)
PSB 440 V section (place marked: main switchboard room)
the end at the PSB is tagged and left coiled at its place
RSP stern ramp starter panel, hydraulic pump room (ELD-51)
Connected 86.7 kW. A breaker is at least 1.25 times the full-load current; a cable is rated for its breaker; no cable loses more than 5 % (the register's rule, checked by ferry/systems/register.py).
IN THE STARTER PANEL (its door opens on them in the model)
Contactors, pump No. 1: main, delta, star
Contactors, pump No. 2: main, delta, star
Relays: cleats open, cleats locked, ramp closed, alarm,
Door lamps: power, pump 1, pump 2, cleat pump, alarm
WHERE THE FEEDS END: the places marked in the machinery spaces
Each place has a yellow outline on its floor, a sign with its tag, and the tagged ends of the cables that
are to be landed on it. The places and sizes are the machinery design basis's (sections 1.2, 2.3, 2.4): a
proposal. Nothing of the switchboards, transformers or generating sets is built.
CONTROL CIRCUIT, 24 V: the control stand's terminal strip X1 (cable W-RMP-10, 30 x 1.5 mm², in conduit E with the pipes)
Emergency stop, contact 1 (opens the pumps' circuit)
Emergency stop, contact 2 (opens the valves' circuit)
Ramp line A pressure, 4 to 20 mA
How it works. T10 in the starter panel makes 24 V. START at the stand pulls in a pump's star-delta starter (K1, K2), which holds itself; STOP drops
it; its auxiliary contact lights PUMP RUNNING. The two levers are spring-centred. CLEATS to OPEN energises V2 b: the two safety latches are lifted and
the ten cleats let go; when all twelve switches say away, CLEATS OPEN lights. RAMP to LOWER energises V1 b, and only then: with a pump's auxiliary
contact closed and relay KA1 (cleats open) pulled in. RAMP to RAISE energises V1 a until the two door switches say the leaf is home (RAMP CLOSED).
CLEATS to LOCK energises V2 a, and only with the ramp closed; all twelve home lights CLEATS LOCKED and goes to the bridge. The emergency stop opens
the pumps' circuit and the valves' circuit: the load-holding valves hold the ramp where it is. The safety latches need no circuit to hold: each falls
in by its own weight. The beacon and the horn run while the ramp is neither locked nor landed. The two indicators are fed by the transmitters PT1 and
CONTROL STAND CS-R: its upstand and its desk, seen by whoever works it (the ramp is to the left)
Each lever is pushed away (LOCK, RAISE) or pulled (OPEN, LOWER) and springs back. The indicators
read 0 to 250 bar with a red mark from 210: SYSTEM about 195 bar with a pump running; RAMP LINE
A nothing with the ramp locked, 68 bar at 30°, 189 bar level, 198 bar at its lowest (sheet 1,
cubicle; its way on is not
cubicle; its way on is not
cubicle; its way on is not
cubicle; its way on is not
cubicle; its way on is not
